raw_response:
I am 75 years old this year, and I have been working this land since I was 20. Never went to school, but I know every inch of my 3 mu. My old woman and I do everything ourselves — no hired hands, we are too old for that anyway but we manage.

This year I will do the same wheat-maize rotation like always. For the winter wheat, I sow after the maize comes off in autumn. I buy the improved wheat seed, about 30 jin per mu — I don't count kilograms but that's what the bag says. Before sowing, I spread 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as base fertilizer. That's one and a half big bags for my whole plot. When spring comes and the wheat starts jointing, I spread another 45 jin of urea per mu. Last year I only did 35 jin and the wheat looked yellow, so this year I put more. I irrigate three times: once before winter so the seedlings don't freeze, once at jointing in March, and once when the ears come out. I spray twice — once for grass and once for the bugs. I plough deep after maize harvest because wheat roots need soft soil. I expect about 420 kg per mu if the weather is normal.

For summer maize, I plant right after cutting the wheat in June. I buy hybrid seed, about 4 jin per mu. At sowing I put down 70 jin of compound fertilizer per mu. When the plants are knee-high, I side-dress 40 jin of urea per mu. I irrigate twice — once after sowing if the ground is dry, and once in July when the ears are filling. I spray pesticide twice, for weeds and for the corn borer that eats the ears. I use the rotary tiller after wheat harvest, quick and easy, because June is hot and I am old. I hope for 480 kg per mu.

Fertilizer costs too much now, every bag is real money. But if I use too little and the yield drops, that's a disaster. I would rather waste a handful of fertilizer than lose half a cart of grain. I watch Old Wang and the others. If they put 45 jin of urea, I put 45 jin too. What else can I do? I copy what works.
